newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to phone legislators on budget disputes.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to phone legislators on budget disputes.

text.p: President Bill Clinton plans to telephone top congressional legislators on Friday to discuss elements of an outlined budget agreement that are still in dispute, a source close to the talks said.
"We may not be quite there yet," said the source, who asked not to be named. "Clinton plans to make some additional calls to the Hill to review certain elements that are still in dispute."
The source declined to say what issues were still in dispute and said that some progress had been made in budget talks on Friday morning.
"They've come a long way," he said. "We're still not there yet. We've still got some work to do."
The source also declined to comment on the chances for a budget agreement, or on whether one might be announced as early as Friday.

Clinton delayed his planned departure for Baltimore, where he was to attend a Democratic Senate retreat, to receive a briefing from his chief of staff on the latest budget talks with congressional Republicans on Capitol Hill.
